text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Romania's Tarom SA state airline plans to create a joint venture with a Western airline, the paper says.
- Romania will turn clocks one hour forward in the first week of October, switching to winter time.
- Former owners of hotels confiscated by the ex-communist regime might claim back their lost properties, the paper says.
- The liquidation of the three refineries earmarked for closure will be carried out gradually, according to the size of their crude oil stocks.

- Some 5,000 tonnes of wheat for export are stored in the Danube port of Braila following the government's failure to print in the Official Gazette a decree to liberalise wheat exports, the paper says.
- Workers made redundant at the Vega, Petrotel and Darmanesti refineries threatened to stage a protest rally in Bucharest on Thursday.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The government allowed state-run Renel RA electricity authority to cut power supplies to 17 loss-making companies earmarked for closure.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The new transport law will become effective starting January 1.
- New plans to restructure the three refineries earmarked for closure might cancel the government's initial decision to shut them down, the paper said.
- Floods damaged scores of households in the counties of Alba, Salaj and Botosani.
- Bad weather might cut Romania's milling wheat crop to some three million tonnes in 1997, compared with initial official estimates of 6.9 million tonnes, the paper says.
General:
ADEVARUL
- The opposition parties plan to ask parliament to call an extraordinary session this month to discuss decrees issued by the government recently.
-- Bucharest newsroom 40-1 3120264
